The second pathway connects Butabarbital to Glutamate receptor ionotropic, kainate 2, which is targeted by Willardiine, also leading to MMP-9. These two distinct pathways suggest that Butabarbital may exert its effects on MMP-9 through different mechanisms, potentially involving different cellular processes. The integration of these pathways highlights the complexity of Butabarbital's interaction with the proteomic landscape, where it may act as a modulator of MMP-9 through either metabolic or receptor-based mechanisms.
